subject.title: fix(repair): publish only validated target commits

question: Should executable repair runners universally require the new Linux namespace and Landlock ABI 3+ boundary, accepting fail-closed repair unavailability on unsupported runners?
rationale: The patch deliberately trades runner compatibility and repair availability for a stronger credential-publication security boundary; tests cannot decide whether that operational contract is acceptable for the maintained fleet.

options.title: Accept after exact-head proof
options.body: Adopt the Linux-only fail-closed contract once hosted proof and required checks pass on 3d80b3a9, with runner prerequisites documented for operators.

options.title: Preserve a compatibility mode
options.body: Keep the hardened mode as the default but design an explicitly configured legacy execution path with clear security warnings and separate validation coverage.

options.title: Pause the redesign
options.body: Do not merge until the publication invariant can be enforced without dropping support for currently deployed execution runners.

recommendation.title: Accept after exact-head proof
recommendation.body: Adopt the Linux-only fail-closed contract once hosted proof and required checks pass on 3d80b3a9, with runner prerequisites documented for operators.

likelyOwner.reason: The sustained repair-boundary work across this PR and its superseded predecessor makes Vincent the strongest available owner to present the final security and runner-compatibility tradeoff.
